original_question: Extend Thurston’s combinatorial theory of critically finite rational maps, where the post-critical set P is finite, to all geometrically finite rational maps. That is, describe such a map f up to combinatorial equivalence relative to P by finite topological data, and characterize which combinatorial types are realized by rational maps.
target_in_paper: Problem 4 in the section "Geometrically finite maps and Kleinian groups," under the subsection "Geometrically finite rational maps."
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper's official formulation. It correctly identifies that the target is to extend Thurston's combinatorial theory from critically finite rational maps to geometrically finite rational maps; it keeps the classification up to combinatorial equivalence relative to the postcritical set P; it asks for a finite amount of topological/combinatorial data; and it includes the realization problem of deciding which combinatorial types arise from rational maps.
missing_details: The ambient object should be stated explicitly: f is a rational self-map of the Riemann sphere.
The paper defines C as the set of critical points, P as the postcritical set P = union over n >= 1 of f^n(C), and J as the Julia set.
The hypothesis "geometrically finite" should be stated exactly as P intersect J is finite.
The paper also gives the equivalent reformulation: every critical point in the Julia set is preperiodic.
The nearby context notes an implicit allowance: rationally indifferent cycles are allowed in the geometrically finite case.
The term "critically finite" should be tied to the paper's usage: these are the maps with |P| < infinity.

If the question is to be fully stand-alone, the phrase "combinatorial equivalence rel P" should be identified as the Thurston-type equivalence by orientation-preserving homeomorphisms isotopic relative to P.
The quantifier is universal: the problem asks for a theory applying to arbitrary geometrically finite rational maps, with no degree restriction stated in the paper.
refined_question: Let f be a rational self-map of the Riemann sphere, with critical set C(f), postcritical set P(f) = union over n >= 1 of f^n(C(f)), and Julia set J(f). Assume that f is geometrically finite in the sense that P(f) intersect J(f) is finite (equivalently, every critical point in J(f) is preperiodic; in particular, rationally indifferent cycles are allowed). Extend Thurston's combinatorial theory for critically finite rational maps, that is, for maps with finite postcritical set |P(f)| < infinity, to this geometrically finite setting: find a finite amount of topological/combinatorial data that determines f up to combinatorial equivalence relative to P(f) in the Thurston sense, and characterize exactly which such combinatorial types are realized by rational maps.
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently: for rational maps f on the Riemann sphere such that every critical point in J(f) is preperiodic, develop a finite topological/combinatorial classification up to combinatorial equivalence relative to P(f), and determine which resulting types are realizable by rational maps.
justification: The draft is essentially a near-verbatim paraphrase of the paper's official Problem 4. The immediately preceding context in the same subsection supplies the needed notation and hidden assumptions: it defines the postcritical set P and Julia set J, defines geometrical finiteness by finiteness of P intersect J, gives the equivalent preperiodicity condition for critical points in J, and explicitly notes that rationally indifferent cycles are allowed. In this arXiv paper there is no Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3; the closest official formulation is this Problem 4.
